rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the centre line at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m (positive = left), all at y = 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is wider than the 8 mm option, so the sensors keep reading the 25 mm tape through small lateral wobble. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, which is the binding limit. Mass 0.8 kg with a 0.16 m body keeps yaw inertia modest, so the robot can turn quickly. Controller: weights are proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal scales with lateral offset and the sign steers toward the tape. kp = 1.5 gives a turn of about 262 PWM per unit of signal, enough to correct offsets without saturating. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd = 0.05 adds mild damping. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80 percent PWM) targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with slalom the likeliest place to show oscillation or line loss. Next measurements: completion_time and progress to check the speed margin, line_loss_events and max_error to test whether the gain is adequate on tight bends, and steering_oscillation to test whether kd is too small.
